title: The Lantern Drift of Silver Creek
verses:
As the twilight descends on the velvet-green peak,
Little Rory guides Benny right down to the creek.
With a bundle of reeds that they crafted with care,
Tilly pauses to catch the cool scent in the air.

Ricky carries bright blossom-boats made out of blue,
While sweet Nia paints wishes in drops of soft dew.
Psittaco tucks a feather of gold on each sail,
As the moon leaves a track like a shimmering trail.

Then they place all six boats on the whispering stream,
Where they float like soft thoughts in a slow-moving dream.
Benny stretches his neck with a satisfied sigh,
Watching tiny lights drift under shadows nearby.

Tilly yawns as the glow-beetles flicker and gleam,
While young Ricky lies down by the edge of the stream.
Psittaco curls his feet in the moss soft and deep,
As the murmuring water sways all things to sleep.

Nia tucks in her wings under stars shining clear,
Rory whispers goodnight to his friends standing near.
All the worries of daytime now vanish and fade,
In the quiet and peace of the cool silver glade.

Now the lanterns drift far to the dark open sea,
Leaving harmony, stillness, and sweet memory.
Close your eyes, little one, let your dreaming begin,
As the night pulls the blanket of slumber right in.
